events.title: Rider Advocate brief: 8 claims (0 void)
events.body:
C1: The driver cancelled as a no-show, but the GPS record shows he was only within 200 m of the pickup point for a cumulative 2 min 55 s before cancelling (F2), which is not more than 3 minutes — so the NS-1 three-part test fails and no cancellation fee is payable. [F2 F4] [NS-0 NS-1 NS-2]
C2: Even measuring from the driver's own "I'm Here" tap at 21:29:45 (41 m from the pickup, F6), he stayed within 200 m for only 1 min 45 s after the tap (F6), far short of the > 3 minutes of continuous waiting at the pickup required by NS-1 (iii). [F6 F4] [NS-1 NS-2]
C3: The platform recorded arrival at 21:28:35 and the cancellation at 21:31:30, i.e. 2 min 55 s after arrival (F5), confirming on the timeline record the same sub-3-minute wait as the GPS — the required > 3:01 never elapsed. [F5 F4] [NS-1 NS-2]
C4: The driver's written claim that he waited at least 5 minutes (F12) and his chat message that he "waited too long" (F10) are contradicted by the GPS and timeline records (F2, F3, F5, F6), so they cannot establish the NS-1 waiting requirement. [F10 F12 F2 F3 F5 F6] [NS-1 NS-2]
C5: Because NS-1 (iii) is not satisfied, the whole $6.61 cancellation fee charged on record (F7, F4) must be refunded in full to the rider. [F7 F4 F2] [NS-1 NS-2 NS-7]
C6: The driver tapped "I'm Here" while inside the pickup radius (41 m, F6), so the NS-2 add-on flag for tapping the button while outside the pickup point does not apply here — I ask only for the fee refund, not a fraud flag. [F6 F1] [NS-1 NS-2]
C7: The rider's own record is clean — 2.6 years on the platform, 4.9 rating, zero disputes and zero upheld complaints in 90 days (F16) — supporting that the rider was not a serial no-show and the fee was wrongly levied. [F16] [NS-2]
C8: There is no traffic or weather excuse for cutting the wait short: no speed band records and no incidents on the route during the trip window, and the weather was fair with 0.0 mm rain (F13, F14, F15). [F13 F14 F15] [NS-1]
Weaknesses: The driver did reach the nearest point 3 m from the pickup at 21:29:20 (F1) and was stationary for 2 min 5 s at 39 m from the pickup (F3), so the other side will argue he genuinely arrived and waited — but the cumulative in-radius time (F2, F6) still falls short of the > 3 minutes NS-1 (iii) requires. | The rider sent no chat message before 21:31 (only the driver's messages F9, F10 exist), so the other side may suggest the rider never responded after the driver's 'I'm here' at 21:29 (F9); this does not cure the short wait requirement but weakens the equities. | The driver's profile shows 1216 trips in 90 days with no upheld disputes (F17), which the other side may use to argue reliability and that the cancellation was out of character.
Asks: refund_full $6.61

events.title: Driver Advocate brief: 7 claims (0 void)
events.body:
D1: The driver did press 'I'm Here' at the pickup point: the timeline records the tap at 21:29:45 and GPS (route-slice fact F1/F3) puts him 41 m from the pickup point at that moment, which is inside the 200 m arrival radius, so NS-1 (i) and (ii) are both satisfied. [F6 F1] [NS-1]
D2: The driver's arrival is corroborated by the platform itself: the platform recorded arrival at 21:28:35 (F5), GPS confirms he was within 200 m from 21:28:35 (F2), and he actually stopped and waited, stationary for 2 min 5 s from 21:29:25 to 21:31:30 only 39 m from the pickup point (F3). [F5 F2 F3] [NS-1]
D3: The only element of NS-1 that is not met is the duration element (iii): the systems record at most 2 min 55 s within 200 m before cancellation (F2) and only 1 min 45 s of waiting after the 'I'm Here' tap (F6), i.e. short of the > 3 minutes required, and no case-specific no-show threshold appears anywhere in the record (F4), so the default three-minute rule applies. [F2 F6 F4] [NS-1]
D4: Because element (iii) fails, the $6.61 cancellation fee cannot stand: NS-2 requires the fee to be refunded in full where any of (i)(ii)(iii) is not fulfilled, and Ryde's own rule in A3 is that the fee is not charged if any condition is unfulfilled (F7, F4). [F7 F4] [NS-2]
D5: The driver's post-trip statement that he 'waited at least 5 minutes at the pickup' (F12) conflicts with the GPS and timeline records (F2, F3, F6) and therefore cannot support the fee; the driver's contemporaneous chat message 'I'm here, white BYD e6' at 21:29 (F9) and 'Cancelling, waited too long' at 21:31 (F10) are the honest record of what he actually did. [F12 F9 F10 F2 F6] [NS-1]
D6: No aggravating account action is warranted here: the driver did not tap 'I'm Here' while outside the pickup radius (tap at 41 m, F6), and his 90-day record shows 0 upheld disputes (F17), so the NS-2 flag for tapping from outside the pickup point does not apply. [F6 F17] [NS-2]
D7: The $6.61 should be refunded as a voucher rather than cash, and the refund request is in time: the fee is on record at $6.61 (F7) with no surge added (F8), and the dispute was filed by the rider on this trip, well inside the 30-day window. [F7 F8] [NS-7]
Weaknesses: The rider's complaint says the driver 'cancelled barely two minutes after arriving' — the system records largely agree: 2 min 55 s within 200 m (F2) and 1 min 45 s after the 'I'm Here' tap (F6), so the driver's own 'waited at least 5 minutes' statement (F12) is contradicted and cannot be relied on. | The driver did in fact cancel a trip for a rider who was charged $6.61 (F4, F7), and the rider has a clean record — 0 disputes, 0 upheld, 4.9 rating (F16) — so there is no basis to attack the rider's credibility. | The driver's text 'Cancelling, waited too long' (F10) reads as the driver abandoning the pickup rather than as a documented no-show, which supports the rider's version; the closest clear GPS approach to the pickup is 3 m only at 21:29:20 (F1), after which he was stationary 39 m away (F3), so he was not at the door. | The three-minute threshold is a data-layer parameter and the record contains no case-specific no-show threshold (F4); if the judge were to read the arrival clock from the platform arrival at 21:28:35 (F5) the wait is still under 3:01, but any rounding or an alternative start point could push it over, which is the driver's principal exposure.
Asks: refund_full $6.61

The driver's arrival is corroborated by the platform itself: the platform recorded arrival at 21:28:35 (F5), GPS confirms he was within 200 m from 21:28:35 (F2), and he actually stopped and waited, stationary for 2 min 5 s from 21:29:25 to 21:31:30 only 39 m from the pickup point (F3).

Because element (iii) fails, the $6.61 cancellation fee cannot stand: NS-2 requires the fee to be refunded in full where any of (i)(ii)(iii) is not fulfilled, and Ryde's own rule in A3 is that the fee is not charged if any condition is unfulfilled (F7, F4).

The driver's post-trip statement that he 'waited at least 5 minutes at the pickup' (F12) conflicts with the GPS and timeline records (F2, F3, F6) and therefore cannot support the fee; the driver's contemporaneous chat message 'I'm here, white BYD e6' at 21:29 (F9) and 'Cancelling, waited too long' at 21:31 (F10) are the honest record of what he actually did.

No aggravating account action is warranted here: the driver did not tap 'I'm Here' while outside the pickup radius (tap at 41 m, F6), and his 90-day record shows 0 upheld disputes (F17), so the NS-2 flag for tapping from outside the pickup point does not apply.

The $6.61 should be refunded as a voucher rather than cash, and the refund request is in time: the fee is on record at $6.61 (F7) with no surge added (F8), and the dispute was filed by the rider on this trip, well inside the 30-day window.

Threshold question (NS-0): the cancellation was made by the driver [F4], so the $6.61 fee can only stand through NS-1; NS-0 routes a driver-cancelled trip claiming rider no-show into NS-1/NS-2 [F4][RD-1][NS-0]. Nothing in this case is a route-deviation case, so no segment findings arise.

NS-1 (i) and (ii) are satisfied: the driver tapped "I'm Here" at 21:29:45 [F6], and at that moment GPS put him 41 m from the pickup point, inside the arrival radius [F6][F1][NS-1]. Both briefs ultimately concede this, and the trace marks it ✓.

NS-1 (iii) fails on the records. After the tap the driver stayed within the pickup radius for only 1 min 45 s (105 s) before cancelling [F6], and his cumulative time within 200 m before cancellation was 2 min 55 s (175 s), measured from the platform arrival confirmation at 21:28:35 to the cancellation at 21:31:30 [F2][F5][F4]. NS-1 (iii) requires continuous waiting at the pickup of more than 3 minutes (≥ 3:01 / > 180 s) [F6][NS-1], so 105 s or 175 s falls short; the record carries no case-specific no-show threshold, so the default three-minute rule applies [F4][NS-1].

The driver's account cannot close that gap: his post-trip statement of "at least 5 minutes" [F12] and his 21:31 message "Cancelling, waited too long" [F10] are contradicted by the GPS and timeline records [F2][F3][F6], and system records (gps / timeline / fare) override statements, so his claim cannot establish the NS-1 wait [F10][F12][NS-1].

Consequence: because element (iii) of NS-1 is unfulfilled, NS-2 requires the $6.61 cancellation fee to be refunded in full, and the fee is on record at exactly $6.61 with no surge [F7][F8][F4][NS-2]. The refund is timely and issues as a voucher, not cash [F7][NS-7]. No departure/route or traffic excuses are in play [F13][F14][F15][NS-1].

No account flag is warranted: the tap at 21:29:45 was 41 m from the pickup [F6], so the driver did not fake arrival from outside the radius, and the trace records no fake confirmation [F6][F1][NS-2]; the driver's 90-day profile (1,216 trips, 0 upheld disputes) [F17] and the rider's clean record [F16] are not relied on to decide the amount, since profile facts never decide a case alone [NS-2]. Both advocates concede refund_full and neither seeks a flag.

events.title: Notices sent to rider and driver
events.body:
RIDER: Your $6.61 cancellation fee is being refunded in full as a Ryde voucher.

We looked at the trip records. The driver cancelled, and he only waited about a minute and 45 seconds at the pickup after marking that he'd arrived — short of the three-minute wait a no-show cancellation needs. His statement that he waited several minutes doesn't match the GPS and timeline records, so the fee can't stand.

Nothing else is needed from you, and no restriction is being placed on your account. The voucher will appear in your Ryde account.

DRIVER: Your cancellation of this trip has been reviewed. The $6.61 cancellation fee is being refunded to the rider as a Ryde voucher.

The records show you marked your arrival, then cancelled after about a minute and 45 seconds at the pickup. A no-show cancellation requires waiting more than three minutes. Your statement about waiting longer isn't supported by the GPS and timeline records, so the fee is not payable.

Your account is not being flagged. This trip and your statement are being passed to RydeHELP for coaching and record.

what_would_change: Had NS-1 (iii) held ((iii) stayed at the pickup more than 3 min after the arrival confirmation, until cancelling (NS-1 default: more than 3 min)), the fee would stand and no refund would be due.

claims.assertion: The driver cancelled as a no-show, but the GPS record shows he was only within 200 m of the pickup point for a cumulative 2 min 55 s before cancelling (F2), which is not more than 3 minutes — so the NS-1 three-part test fails and no cancellation fee is payable.

Even measuring from the driver's own "I'm Here" tap at 21:29:45 (41 m from the pickup, F6), he stayed within 200 m for only 1 min 45 s after the tap (F6), far short of the > 3 minutes of continuous waiting at the pickup required by NS-1 (iii).

The platform recorded arrival at 21:28:35 and the cancellation at 21:31:30, i.e. 2 min 55 s after arrival (F5), confirming on the timeline record the same sub-3-minute wait as the GPS — the required > 3:01 never elapsed.

The driver's written claim that he waited at least 5 minutes (F12) and his chat message that he "waited too long" (F10) are contradicted by the GPS and timeline records (F2, F3, F5, F6), so they cannot establish the NS-1 waiting requirement.
Because NS-1 (iii) is not satisfied, the whole $6.61 cancellation fee charged on record (F7, F4) must be refunded in full to the rider.

The driver tapped "I'm Here" while inside the pickup radius (41 m, F6), so the NS-2 add-on flag for tapping the button while outside the pickup point does not apply here — I ask only for the fee refund, not a fraud flag.

The rider's own record is clean — 2.6 years on the platform, 4.9 rating, zero disputes and zero upheld complaints in 90 days (F16) — supporting that the rider was not a serial no-show and the fee was wrongly levied.

There is no traffic or weather excuse for cutting the wait short: no speed band records and no incidents on the route during the trip window, and the weather was fair with 0.0 mm rain (F13, F14, F15).

weaknesses: The driver did reach the nearest point 3 m from the pickup at 21:29:20 (F1) and was stationary for 2 min 5 s at 39 m from the pickup (F3), so the other side will argue he genuinely arrived and waited — but the cumulative in-radius time (F2, F6) still falls short of the > 3 minutes NS-1 (iii) requires.

The rider sent no chat message before 21:31 (only the driver's messages F9, F10 exist), so the other side may suggest the rider never responded after the driver's 'I'm here' at 21:29 (F9); this does not cure the short wait requirement but weakens the equities.
The driver's profile shows 1216 trips in 90 days with no upheld disputes (F17), which the other side may use to argue reliability and that the cancellation was out of character.

claims.assertion: The driver did press 'I'm Here' at the pickup point: the timeline records the tap at 21:29:45 and GPS (route-slice fact F1/F3) puts him 41 m from the pickup point at that moment, which is inside the 200 m arrival radius, so NS-1 (i) and (ii) are both satisfied.

The driver's arrival is corroborated by the platform itself: the platform recorded arrival at 21:28:35 (F5), GPS confirms he was within 200 m from 21:28:35 (F2), and he actually stopped and waited, stationary for 2 min 5 s from 21:29:25 to 21:31:30 only 39 m from the pickup point (F3).

The only element of NS-1 that is not met is the duration element (iii): the systems record at most 2 min 55 s within 200 m before cancellation (F2) and only 1 min 45 s of waiting after the 'I'm Here' tap (F6), i.e. short of the > 3 minutes required, and no case-specific no-show threshold appears anywhere in the record (F4), so the default three-minute rule applies.

Because element (iii) fails, the $6.61 cancellation fee cannot stand: NS-2 requires the fee to be refunded in full where any of (i)(ii)(iii) is not fulfilled, and Ryde's own rule in A3 is that the fee is not charged if any condition is unfulfilled (F7, F4).

The driver's post-trip statement that he 'waited at least 5 minutes at the pickup' (F12) conflicts with the GPS and timeline records (F2, F3, F6) and therefore cannot support the fee; the driver's contemporaneous chat message 'I'm here, white BYD e6' at 21:29 (F9) and 'Cancelling, waited too long' at 21:31 (F10) are the honest record of what he actually did.

No aggravating account action is warranted here: the driver did not tap 'I'm Here' while outside the pickup radius (tap at 41 m, F6), and his 90-day record shows 0 upheld disputes (F17), so the NS-2 flag for tapping from outside the pickup point does not apply.

The $6.61 should be refunded as a voucher rather than cash, and the refund request is in time: the fee is on record at $6.61 (F7) with no surge added (F8), and the dispute was filed by the rider on this trip, well inside the 30-day window.

weaknesses: The rider's complaint says the driver 'cancelled barely two minutes after arriving' — the system records largely agree: 2 min 55 s within 200 m (F2) and 1 min 45 s after the 'I'm Here' tap (F6), so the driver's own 'waited at least 5 minutes' statement (F12) is contradicted and cannot be relied on.

The driver did in fact cancel a trip for a rider who was charged $6.61 (F4, F7), and the rider has a clean record — 0 disputes, 0 upheld, 4.9 rating (F16) — so there is no basis to attack the rider's credibility.

The driver's text 'Cancelling, waited too long' (F10) reads as the driver abandoning the pickup rather than as a documented no-show, which supports the rider's version; the closest clear GPS approach to the pickup is 3 m only at 21:29:20 (F1), after which he was stationary 39 m away (F3), so he was not at the door.

The three-minute threshold is a data-layer parameter and the record contains no case-specific no-show threshold (F4); if the judge were to read the arrival clock from the platform arrival at 21:28:35 (F5) the wait is still under 3:01, but any rounding or an alternative start point could push it over, which is the driver's principal exposure.

points.response: Conceded as to (i) and (ii): the driver's 'I'm Here' tap at 21:29:45 was 41 m from the pickup (F6), inside the 200 m arrival radius, so NS-1 (i) and (ii) are met — but that only narrows the case to element (iii), which fails.

The platform arrival at 21:28:35 (F5) and the stationary spell 39 m away (F3) show presence, not compliance: cumulative time within 200 m before cancellation was only 2 min 55 s (F2), so the arrival evidence the driver relies on is precisely what proves the wait was too short.

Agreed, and this is the whole case: at most 2 min 55 s within 200 m (F2) and only 1 min 45 s after the tap (F6), with no case-specific threshold recorded (F4), so the default rule applies and the > 3 minutes required by NS-1 (iii) was never reached.

Agreed — NS-2 mandates full refund of the $6.61 charged on record (F7, F4) once element (iii) is unfulfilled; the driver's brief and mine ask for the same outcome, and the rider's complaint (cancellation barely two minutes after arriving) matches the system records.

Agreed that the driver's 'waited at least 5 minutes' statement (F12) is defeated by the GPS and timeline records (F2, F3, F6), and his own 21:31 message 'Cancelling, waited too long' (F10) confirms he abandoned the pickup before the threshold — so the fee cannot be sustained.

I do not seek any account flag against the driver: his tap was inside the radius (F6) and his 90-day record shows 0 upheld disputes (F17), so the NS-2 add-on flag is unnecessary — I ask only for the fee back.

Agreed on mechanism: the $6.61 is on record with no surge added (F7, F8) and the dispute is timely, so refund_full of $6.61 — issued as a Ryde voucher per NS-7 — is the correct and now uncontested disposition.

Conceded as to the arithmetic: the driver's cumulative time within 200 m before cancelling was 2 min 55 s (F2), which does not exceed the 3 minutes NS-1 (iii) requires, so the fee cannot be supported on that element.
Conceded: after the 'I'm Here' tap at 21:29:45 the driver remained within 200 m for only 1 min 45 s (F6), which is short of the > 3 minutes NS-1 (iii) requires and cannot be cured by any other fact.
Conceded: the timeline shows platform-recorded arrival at 21:28:35 and cancellation at 21:31:30, i.e. 2 min 55 s (F5, F4), so no reading of this record reaches > 3:01 of waiting.

Conceded: the driver's post-trip statement of a five-minute wait (F12) and his 'waited too long' message (F10) are contradicted by the GPS and timeline records (F2, F3, F5, F6), and under the system-records-first rule his statement cannot establish the NS-1 waiting requirement.

Do not contest the amount or the direction: the fee on record is $6.61 (F7) and NS-2 mandates full refund where any NS-1 element fails, so I ask the judge to order refund_full of $6.61 under NS-2, payable as a voucher per NS-7.

Agreed, and I ask the judge to record it expressly: the 'I'm Here' tap at 41 m (F6) was inside the pickup radius shown by GPS (F1), so the NS-2 account-flag add-on for tapping while outside the pickup point does not apply and my client should not be sent to account review on this incident.

No dispute on the rider's record (F16); the driver's record is likewise unblemished — 1,216 trips in 90 days with 0 upheld disputes (F17) — so this was an honest but premature no-show judgement, not a fee-extraction pattern.

Accepted, and I would add that fair weather and no incidents or speed-band records (F13, F14, F15) were never offered by my client as an excuse; he simply miscounted the wait, and the fee must fall on the records alone.
